abstract: As a semi-aquatic plant, rice (Oryza sativa L.) has evolved adaptive traits to withstand prolonged submergence, among which the formation of adventitious roots (ARs) is particularly critical. However, the regulatory mechanisms governing AR development remain poorly understood. The developmental divergence of the two morphologically distinct AR types, AR1 (thin) and AR2 (thick), also remains unclear. In this study, we demonstrate that AR1 and AR2 undergo distinct developmental pathways prior to emergence. AR1 shows a more prolonged pre-emergence growth trajectory than AR2, and its growth may be related to the vascular bundle architecture. Although the leaf sheath encases AR2, it delays emergence while simultaneously promoting thickening, mainly by increasing cortical cell layer numbers and cortical cell area. Through systematic comparison of the developmental processes of these two AR types combined with comparative transcriptomic analysis, we identified candidate genes potentially involved in AR type development. Our transcriptomic analysis of nodal tissues at AR emergence sites revealed that OsWOX11 regulates total AR number primarily by promoting AR2 development. Although the OsWOX11 coding sequence is highly conserved across rice accessions, its promoter region exhibits substantial natural variation, raising the possibility that promoter polymorphisms could influence AR development. Functional assays revealed that the haplotype 3 (Hap3) promoter variant drives markedly higher transcriptional activity relative to haplotype 1 (Hap1). The Hap3 promoter variant represents a candidate genetic resource that warrants further investigation in the context of AR development and flooding resilience.
